title: Hymn and Bell
premise: Cyrus Vasquez, a meticulous new teacher at Hollowmere School, begins documenting the strange pattern of students who vanish from class and return hollowed out, their memories of the missing hours gone. His audio recordings of the school's night hours reveal a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud, and he learns that decades ago the school's founders invited something in to keep the community 'whole.' With the help of Marisol, the night custodian who remembers what others forgot, Cyrus must decide whether to expose the ritual and break the town's fragile belonging, or preserve it and lose the students forever. In the end he burns the founders' ledger at dawn, unbinding the entity, but the price is his own documented memories, which the entity takes as it leaves, leaving him a stranger who keeps a notebook he can no longer read.
about_author: Ivo Montrose is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in small-town classrooms before turning to horror. They write about institutions that love their people too much to let them go.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Cyrus Vasquez arrives at Hollowmere School and begins his first week, documenting everything in his notebook as a private ritual of control. He notices the faculty's unnerving cheerfulness and a gap in the attendance ledger for October. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cautious hope shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: A student, Wren, is absent; when she returns the next day she is pleasant but cannot remember the day at all, and neither can anyone else. Cyrus's documentation instinct sharpens into unease. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: first crack in the school's polished surface.

chapters.title: Night Custodian
chapters.summary: Cyrus stays late grading and meets Marisol, the night custodian, who warns him not to record in the building after dark, then contradicts herself by asking if he hears it too. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: an unexpected alliance forming in the dark.

chapters.title: Recording One
chapters.summary: Ignoring the warning, Cyrus leaves a recorder running overnight in his classroom. The playback captures footsteps, a hymn hummed off-key, and a voice asking questions to no one. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: fascination tipping into dread.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: On the third night's recording, a second voice answers the questions, flat and patient, and the answers make Cyrus's skin crawl: it knows the students' names, including Wren's. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the horror of confirmation.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's History
chapters.summary: Cyrus digs through the school archive and finds a founders' ledger from 1931 describing a 'Covenant of Wholeness' and a bell that must be rung at every solstice. Pages after 1974 are missing. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: scholarly dread, the past pressing close.

chapters.title: Marisol's Memory
chapters.summary: Marisol confesses she was a student here in the seventies; she lost a brother to the 'missing days' and is the only one who still remembers him. She shows Cyrus the old bell tower, sealed since 1974. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: grief as resistance.

chapters.title: The Roster
chapters.summary: Cyrus cross-references decades of attendance ledgers and finds the pattern: every generation, a handful of students vanish for a day and return diminished, and the school's test scores and town fortunes rise afterward. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: sick clarity, the town's prosperity built on theft.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren, sensing Cyrus knows, comes to him after class and asks what's wrong with her. He lies badly. That night her name appears in the ledger's new entries, written in no one's handwriting. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: a child's fear reaching for an adult's honesty.

chapters.title: The Principal's Kindness
chapters.summary: Principal Aldous invites Cyrus to dinner, warmly explains that Hollowmere 'takes care of its own,' and gently suggests he stop keeping records. Cyrus realizes the faculty know and consent. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love against duty, the temptation of belonging.

chapters.title: Solstice Approaches
chapters.summary: The town decorates for the Winter Solstice festival; the sealed bell tower has been unsealed and cleaned. Cyrus counts the names in the ledger: this year's covenant requires five, and four are already chosen. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: Marisol translates the ledger's Latin: in 1931 the founders, starving after a failed harvest, invited 'the Keeper of Wholeness' to feed on memory in exchange for the town's survival, sealed by the bell's toll. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: the horror of a desperate bargain made lovingly.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Cyrus's documentation disappears: his notebook pages blank, his recordings wiped, his emails purged. Only the copy he hid with Marisol survives. He understands the school is editing him. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the terror of losing proof of oneself.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: The ledger completes itself: the fifth name is Cyrus's own. The Keeper has noticed the one who watches. Marisol urges him to flee before the solstice. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: fear wrestling with the duty to stay.

chapters.title: Fugue
chapters.summary: Cyrus loses six hours and wakes in the bell tower with chalk on his hands and a circle drawn on the floor; he cannot account for any of it, and his handwriting fills the margins with the phrase 'we are whole.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the enemy is inside his own hours.

chapters.title: Wren's Plan
chapters.summary: Wren, half-hollow already, reveals she can hear the Keeper's questions in her sleep and has learned its rules: it must answer truthfully when asked in the bell's presence, and it cannot take what is freely surrendered. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the victim becoming the strategist.

chapters.title: The Faculty
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts the teachers; Aldous admits they were all taken once, that the missing hours are the price of the town's happiness, and begs him not to make the children grieve what they'll never remember. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: compassion weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Snow, candles, the whole town singing the off-key hymn from the recordings. Cyrus and Marisol break into the bell tower with Wren and the ledger as the four chosen children are led in by their smiling parents. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love against duty at its sharpest.

chapters.title: The Tolling
chapters.summary: The Keeper manifests as a second voice from every mouth at once and demands the covenant be sealed; Cyrus rings the broken bell himself and asks it the truth: what was given, what was taken, and what it truly is. It answers, and the answers unmake the town's comfortable story. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax, truth as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: The Keeper, bound by its own rules, offers a trade: the children go free if a documented memory is freely surrendered in their place. Cyrus offers his notebooks, his records, every proof of who he has been, and Wren witnesses the surrender. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the ultimate act of documentation.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn breaks; the children wake remembering everything, and the town reels with collective grief and guilt as the stolen years return in fragments. Marisol remembers her brother fully at last. Cyrus stands in the tower, holding a notebook written in his own hand that means nothing to him. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Hymn and Bell
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Hollowmere mourns honestly for the first time in ninety years. Wren tutors the memory-bewildered Cyrus, reading his old notes aloud to him like stories about a stranger he might have liked. He begins a new notebook; the first line is her name. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth instead of theft.
